The GJK algorithm is a computational geometry algorithm used to determine if two convex shapes intersect. It works by iteratively constructing a simplex (a generalization of a triangle in higher dimensions) that encloses the origin. If the origin is inside the simplex, the shapes intersect. If the simplex cannot be expanded to include the origin, the shapes do not intersect. The algorithm is efficient and widely used in collision detection for video games and physics simulations.
